title: Constrained electrothermal design space exploration of a three dimensional busbar
research_question: How can uncertainty aware adaptive sampling reduce COMSOL evaluations while finding low mass and low loss busbar designs that satisfy electrothermal constraints?

drive_definition.required_model_change: Replace or supplement the fixed potential boundary with a terminal current parameter so geometry candidates are compared at the same electrical load.
drive_definition.migration_check: At the baseline geometry and approximately 160 A, the current driven model must reproduce the 20 mV baseline within declared numerical tolerances.

objectives.name: copper_mass_kg
objectives.source: COMSOL geometry volume multiplied by copper density

constraints.name: maximum_temperature
constraints.note: This is a study constraint, not a certification limit. It must be replaced or justified for a specific product and insulation class.

constraints.name: maximum_current_density
constraints.expression: Jmax <= 1.10 * Jmax_baseline at the same current
constraints.note: An absolute product limit requires conductor, cooling, lifetime and standard-specific evidence.

fixed_assumptions: Copper busbar body and titanium bolt material definitions remain unchanged in version 1
No radiation, contact resistance, bolt preload, structural mechanics or thermal expansion in version 1
Boundary roles remain electrically and thermally equivalent after geometry rebuild
All final Pareto candidates require fresh COMSOL verification
completion_criteria: The current driven baseline reproduces the original baseline electrical and thermal outputs within documented tolerances.
Every decision variable changes the rebuilt COMSOL geometry without invalid entity selections.
Every required output is exported with units and provenance.
At least one feasible Pareto improvement is confirmed by a fresh COMSOL solve.
Independent domain and out of domain test sets remain untouched until final evaluation.
